balance_notes: GDD 4.1 shipping-slice reachability, the audit's second failure: fuel_capacity_kg goes 1200 -> 1900 and thrust_n 26400 -> 35200 with fuel_burn_kgs 12.0 -> 16.0, which holds exhaust velocity at 35200/16 = 2200 m/s exactly as before, so only the tank size and the thrust level move and the engine's efficiency is untouched. Ideal delta-v at base rises from 2200*ln(2100/900) = 1864 m/s to 2200*ln(2800/900) = 2497 m/s, a gain of 633 m/s against a measured suborbital shortfall of 290.17 kg (the fuel that ascent needed and did not have, which at the old wet mass is 2200*ln(2390/900) - 1864 = 284 m/s). The extra thrust is the second half of the fix rather than decoration: liftoff thrust-to-weight goes 26400/(2100*4) = 3.14 to 35200/(2800*4) = 3.14, i.e. the bigger tank is carried at the same acceleration it had before, so the 58% larger propellant load does not buy itself extra gravity loss. Burn time to depletion is 1900/16 = 118.8 s against 1200/12 = 100 s.

GDD 2.3.5 full-hold mass doubling: dry_mass_kg 900 and base_slots 6 are unchanged, and the Debris Designer's recomputed shipping-slice figure is 150.27 kg per crushed-equivalent slot (49290 kg-slots over 328 slots across suborbital and low). A full base hold is 6 * 150.27 = 901.6 kg against a 900 kg staged dry ship, i.e. 2.002x. That is measured on the catalog as it stands, not asserted. Note that base_slots is the number the GDD's own walkthrough puts on screen ('Cargo reads 4 of 6') and I have deliberately not moved it to make any other check pass.

GDD 2.3.1 ablation optimum, the audit's first failure, re-derived rather than re-asserted. The audit reports the flown cooling as roughly a fifth of the claimed [1.0, 0.92, 0.87, 0.86]; applied element-wise to the claimed reductions (8/13/14 percent -> 1.6/2.6/2.8 percent) that is skim_heat_multiplier [1.0, 0.984, 0.974, 0.972], which is what I have adopted. At the fixed cubic law the entry-heat saving from skimming is therefore only 1 - 0.984^3 = 4.72% of the direct-entry cost for the first skim, a further 2.88% for the second and 0.57% for the third. A U-curve still exists, but only if the per-skim price is smaller than those savings, so I re-derived all three knobs the audit named plus skim_peak: cycle_toll_base_pct 1.42 -> 0.16, cycle_toll_growth 1.25 -> 1.35, heat_cost_coefficient 0.00002 -> 0.000018, skim_peak 40 -> 29. heat_index and heat_cost_exponent are unchanged. The per-skim price is then toll_i + 0.000018*29^3 = toll_i + 0.4390, i.e. 0.6550 for the first skim and 0.7306 for the second, and the savings are 0.0472*30.333 = 1.4325 and 0.0288*30.333 = 0.8721 from the high band, 0.8503 and 0.5175 from the low band, 0.4862 and 0.2959 from suborbital. Every skim whose saving exceeds its price is taken and no other, which lands the optimum at 2 skims from high, 1 from low and 0 from suborbital, and cost_curve is that model evaluated: high [30.49, 29.72, 29.57, 30.23], low [18.16, 17.96, 18.18, 18.91], suborbital [10.45, 10.62, 11.06, 11.83]. Worked example anyone can check: high k=2 = 0.000018*(119*0.974)^3 + (0.16 + 0.216 + 0.2916) + 2*0.4390 = 28.0279 + 0.6676 + 0.8780 = 29.57.

Flagged for the human under GDD 4.5 risk 1, because it is a design finding and not a tuning one: at the measured cooling the U-curve is real but shallow. The high band's optimum beats a single plunge by 0.92 plate-percent and beats one skim by 0.15, and the low band's optimum beats a plunge by 0.20. The audit's own suggestion allowed for escalation on the grounds that no toll setting produces a U at the measured cooling; that is true if only the toll moves, and it stops being true once heat_cost_coefficient and skim_peak move with it, which is the path I took. But a 0.15-percent difference between one skim and two is arithmetic the player cannot feel, so the mechanic is currently correct and invisible. The honest levers are upstream of me and both are in the GDD: make skims actually cool the entry more (deeper skims at 40-45 km periapsis, per the Researcher's own dv table, where a pass is worth 25-85 m/s rather than a feather), or accept 4.5's stated fallback of a flat toll with a hard pass cap. If the simulator can report the exact per-band skim_heat_multiplier arrays rather than a single ratio, I will price those instead of a fifth-of-claimed estimate.

GDD 2.3.2 parachute at full hold: descent_speed_full_hold_ms 4.6 sits just under the 5.0 m/s soft-landing line for a staged 900 kg ship carrying a full 900 kg base hold, i.e. 1800 kg. Because terminal speed goes as sqrt(m), the same canopy brings an empty staged ship down at 4.6/sqrt(2) = 3.25 m/s, and a greedy hold rather than a legal-average one crosses the line: three docking collars from the low band is 1665 kg of cargo, 2565 kg total, 4.6*sqrt(2565/1800) = 5.49 m/s and a hard landing. That gap is exactly what the Parachute upgrade is sold against - tier 1 at 3.9 m/s restores a 1665 kg haul to 4.66 m/s. The implied canopy at parachute_drag_coefficient 1.8 is A = 2*1800*4/(0.6*1.8*4.6^2) = 630 m2, which is the same size the Researcher derived (343 m2 at Cd 1.4 for a 900 kg ship at 5 m/s) scaled for twice the mass.

GDD 2.3.6 lazy-run break-even: launch_cost 100 is 2.5 pieces of the cheapest junk in the game (a suborbital small solid prices at 1.0 * 40 = 40), which is the 'about the value of 2-3 pieces of cheap junk' clause read literally. A lazy run is six suborbital smalls, 240, minus 100 launch and minus the re-plating bill for the band's optimal descent, 10.45% * 3 = 31, for a profit of 109. The same run flown badly - a direct plunge is only 10.45 vs 10.62 percent here, so laziness in the descent costs almost nothing at this band - still clears the launch. A full low-band hold of solids is 576 to 648 before the 17.96% re-plate (54), so the band change roughly quadruples the profit per run, which is what paces the upgrade tree.

GDD 2.3.4 no shear under steady tow: steady-state tension in one cable is that piece's mass times the astronaut's acceleration, and that acceleration is already suppressed by everything on the line, so tension = F * m_i / (110 + sum m) <= F * m_i / (110 + m_i) < F = 400 N for any load whatsoever. The worst legal case in the whole catalog is a single momentum_wheel_cluster at 715 kg: 400 * 715/825 = 346.7 N. In the shipping slice it is a single docking_collar at 555 kg: 400 * 555/665 = 333.8 N. Adding the second collar lowers per-cable tension to 555 * 400/1220 = 182 N, which is the design's stated inversion - a heavy load is sluggish, not fragile. magnet_hold_force_n 900 clears the worst case by 2.6x, so nothing steady can ever shear and the whole shear budget belongs to latch jerk and swing jerk.

GDD 2.3.3 tow fee: free_radius_m 1200 is one screen at the game's scale, the fee is zero inside it, and beyond it the fraction is 0.5 * (d - 1200) / (628319 - 1200) clamped to [0, 0.5], where 628319 m is half the circumference of the Researcher's 200 km planet. It reaches exactly 0.5 at the antipode, cannot exceed it, cannot go negative, and is charged off the haul rather than the balance, so it never touches savings.

Upgrade pacing and the one thing I could not verify: the tier-1 set totals 2800 and the tier-2 set 6700, which at roughly 110 profit per suborbital run and 450 to 550 per low-band run paces the twelve purchases across about 20-24 runs. fuel_tank tier 1 raises delta-v to 2200*ln(3300/900) = 2858 m/s, tier 2 to 2200*ln(4000/900) = 3283 m/s. The audit asked me to re-check that fuel_tank tier 1 stays a wanted purchase rather than a prerequisite, and I cannot settle that from here: the flown ascent cost of the low band was never measured, only its failure, so I do not know whether 2497 m/s at base already reaches it. I have sized the base tank for the reachability requirement, which is the hard check, and if the next sweep shows the low band opening at base config the fix is to take fuel_capacity_kg back toward 1600 rather than to touch thrust, since thrust is what is holding the ascent's gravity losses flat.
